rationale: Completes the knowledge-correction review for the main account and restores the gap-3 answer in the same record. No execution was requested and nothing new was run: the parent account is rewritten as a successor with the same conclusion, witnesses, controls and limitations, plus (a) an explicit correction review of knowledge e65d63f4057d4c5bbe8390ac06b30fce-knowledge-2 revision 2, which this account already cites and which class (5) of the account is itself the record of, (b) the settlement, as far as the evidence allows, of the two variants the parent discriminator named: the peers that receive a forwarded compaction each recompute the bound against their own decided index and build from their own range, so they are read to mirror the leader's loss rather than to reach a different state, while the trim path cannot raise a compacted index above a live replica's reported accepted index at all because its bound is the minimum recorded accepted index, and (c) answers to this investigation's two registered gaps: gap-3 as resolved by the drift-bound receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4, whose explanation is restated here because the previous parent account lost it when it was rewritten, and gap-5 as resolved by this review. The two child accounts affected by the same correction were reviewed and answered in the previous turn (70b664b22f6b450983690d78fddad184-interpretation-0 and -interpretation-1), and the trim child's gap about a request below an over-compacted index stays open with its recorded partial progress. Incomplete and unexecuted: the forwarded-compaction peer variant, the direct-range-read and store-level-trim routes below a compacted index, and a delivery of a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot to a NoSnapshot instance.

interpretations.rationale: One index-space error in the StopSign accounting, six witnessed classes of consequence in ten receipts of one lineage, and the drift is neither bounded nor repaired inside the sealed configuration. Cause: sync_log adds the StopSign carried by a LogSync on top of sync_idx plus the suffix length while the sender's resume point may already count that StopSign, and create_log_sync never shifts sync_idx for a StopSign the sender already holds. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and is given a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: follower after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), follower re-promising in an ordinary new term with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), the leader that takes over from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13), and two followers under a snapshot-capable entry type (fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 51, 52). Each such replica stops reporting its reconfiguration as decided and its decided-log read loses the entries (one element or nothing against six before). (2) The index drifts one step per re-synchronization round rather than settling: three consecutive reconnection rounds took the followers from 7 to 8 to 9 over unchanged content and the leader's decided index followed (6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 41-49). (3) A write quorum of drifted reports makes the leader decide the reported index although it holds fewer entries (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24; snapshot-capable: fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 event 53), after which the leader no longer reports the reconfiguration as decided and its decided log is unreadable. This decision needs two drifted reporters in a three-node cluster: with one, the leader stayed consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9). (4) Both compaction paths inherit the drifted values and act on them: trim(None) took the minimum recorded accepted index, which had drifted above the leader's content, and compacted index 7 for a log of six indices, with the region then reported trimmed (ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a events 9-15); snapshot(Some(8), false) was accepted inside the drifted decided index, advanced the compacted index to 8 and produced a snapshot holding none of the five decided entries the log contained, so the entries are no longer reachable and the snapshot that represents them is empty (e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c events 0-5). Both calls returned success on input the documentation allows. (5) The drift neither saturates nor is repaired, and it does not crash the replicas (2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4). From the healthy baseline of accepted 6 / decided 6 with a readable six-element decided log on all three nodes (events 9-11), eight further rounds of the same two-follower re-synchronization took both followers to accepted 14 / decided 14, one index per round with no saturation (events 12, 13, 18, 19, 33, 34), while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index followed to 14 with its decided-log read returning nothing in every round, from the first round on (events 14, 20, 35). A leader change was then performed onto node 1, one of the inflated followers: it took the lead in a new term and still reported accepted 14 and decided 14 instead of re-deriving its six indices of content (event 36), node 2 reported accepted 15 against decided 14 and node 3 -- the previously truthful leader, which held six indices -- was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7 (events 37, 38), so the drift spread to the replica that had stayed honest rather than being repaired. The three following rounds left the new leader at accepted 14 / decided 14 and took node 2 to accepted 16, 17, 18 and node 3 to accepted 8, 9, 10 while the decided index stayed at 14 (events 39-47): once no write quorum of recorded accepted indexes covers the further reports the decided index stops following, so the later drift appears as accepted indexes that never reach a decision, and the leader's decided index remains thirteen indices above the content it holds and its decided-log read remains unusable (node 2 read an empty decided log at events 45, 46, 47). No guarded drain, sample or leader change panicked over the eleven rounds (event 48: rounds 11, panics 0, 154 messages delivered). Comparisons 0-4 of that receipt are violated with witnesses 33, 34, 35 and 36 (the fifth additionally records nodes 2 and 3 as outside its applicability); comparisons 5-7 came out unknown because their declared admissions put a node condition on the prerequisite and a node-less identity on the panic event, so those states are asserted from the sampled events named above rather than from comparison outcomes. (6) With the snapshot-capable entry type the compaction consequence reaches a lagging replica as an installed but empty snapshot (0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25). After three re-synchronization rounds the nodes reported accepted 9 / decided 9, accepted 10 / decided 9 and accepted 6 / decided 9, with decided-log reads of 1, 0 and nothing (events 148-150); the leader change onto node 1 left the decided index at 9 (events 152-154), the local snapshot inside that drifted decided index completed with compacted index 8 and a snapshot holding zero ids (event 155), and the re-synchronization of the replica whose reported accepted index lay below the compacted index raised no panic (event 162) but installed that complete snapshot and no suffix, leaving the replica at accepted 10 / decided 10 with a decided-log read of two entries where the configuration decided six, while the same exchange moved the leader's decided index from 9 to 10 (events 159-161). Reading only that case's own samples: the drift-driven compaction turned into a silent property loss on a replica rather than into an error or a crash. Correction review: this account already cites the drift knowledge at revision 2, whose narrowed claim is that the reported accepted index drifts one further index per round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum of drifted reports covers it; class (5) is precisely the record of that boundary, and every decided value used above is sampled in its own receipt rather than inferred from an unbounded following, so the correction changes neither the conclusion nor the witness set, and the two affected child accounts were reviewed the same way (70b664b22f6b450983690d78fddad184-interpretation-0 and -interpretation-1). Variants settled as far as the evidence allows: the peers that receive a forwarded Compaction::Snapshot each recompute the requested bound against their own decided index and build their snapshot from their own range (create_log_sync and create_diff_snapshot are per-node operations), so with the same drifted decided index they are read to mirror the leader's loss rather than to reach a different state - no run sampled that, because every observed compaction was requested with local_only = true or on the leader itself; and the trim path cannot raise a compacted index above a live replica's reported accepted index at all, since its bound is the minimum recorded accepted index, which is why the trim child's accounts treat that route as unreachable in-cluster. Controls: the pre-change samples and the no-reconnect control kept six indices of content, a six-element decided log, the StopSign at its own index and the reconfiguration reported as decided (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11, 19-21; 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d events 38-40; fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 events 48-50; 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 9-11; 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 238-240).

838461385f784f74af057837ff488a66-gap-3.explanation: Resolved by the drift-bound receipt 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4: nothing inside the sealed configuration bounds or repairs the drift within the tested range. Eight further re-synchronization rounds added exactly one index per round to both followers (accepted 7 at events 12, 13 up to accepted 14 at events 33, 34) over unchanged content while the leader's own accepted index stayed 6 and its decided index followed to 14 with an unreadable decided log in every round (events 14, 20, 35). The leader change was not a repair: the new leader kept its inflated accepted index of 14 instead of re-deriving six (event 36), and the replica that had stayed truthful was itself re-synchronized to accepted 7 (event 38). The following rounds took the followers to accepted 16, 17, 18 and 8, 9, 10 while the decided index froze at 14 (events 39-47), so the only bound on the decided index in this pattern is quorum arithmetic rather than an explicit limit, and no counter, storage guard or automatic repair was observed. Eleven guarded stages with 154 delivered messages produced zero panics (event 48), so the unrepaired drift is silent: every call succeeded and no endpoint reported an error. The later narrowing of the drift knowledge does not touch this answer.

ebbec352695d43beb398bb1b239cda41-gap-5.explanation: Reviewed and unchanged. This account already reads the narrowed premise: the reported accepted index drifts one further index per re-synchronization round, while the decided index follows only while a write quorum of drifted reports covers it, and class (5) is the record of where that following stops (decided frozen at 14 while reported accepted indexes reached 18 and 10). Every decided value cited above comes from the receipt that sampled it, so no claim in this account depended on the unbounded following that the correction narrowed. The two accounts the correction listed as live uses were reviewed the same way in the same round (the trim child at 70b664b22f6b450983690d78fddad184-interpretation-0 and the snapshot child at -interpretation-1): both keep their conclusions, both re-read the use at revision 2, and their own gaps are answered there.

knowledge.assertion: sync_log adds the carried StopSign on top of sync_idx plus the suffix, and each further re-synchronization adds another index
the decided-log read loses the entries after such a re-synchronization
the condition is the resume point covering the StopSign's index
the leader decides the reported accepted index without bounding it to its own log
a candidate leader syncing from a follower is inflated in its own accepted index
the reported accepted index drifts one index per re-synchronization round while the decided index follows only while a write quorum covers it
trim accepted a drifted bound and compacted past the content the leader held
the snapshot path accepted a drifted bound and produced a snapshot holding none of the entries
a replica re-synchronized below the compacted index receives a complete snapshot built from the empty range

counterevidence: The no-reconnect control kept every endpoint consistent (accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, six-element decided read: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 events 9-11; 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 9-11; 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 events 238-240), and in the newterm case the new leader and the node that received nothing stayed consistent (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 events 9, 10), so the deviation follows a re-synchronization whose resume point covers the StopSign.

The leader-side decision at a drifted index requires a write quorum of drifted reporters in one term (two of three nodes); one drifted reporter left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9), and in the drift-bound receipt the decided index stopped advancing once the reports outran every write quorum (2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 events 46, 47 against decided 14).

The compaction consequences need the drift to cover every node the bound is derived from: trim's bound is the minimum recorded value, so a truthful replica would keep it honest (76cabb0efc3b4eda8eda8c9c79025550-interpretation-0), and the snapshot witness used a request strictly inside the drifted decided index because the StopSign equal case lowers the bound.

The documented reconfiguration flow expects a new instance once a node observes StopSign(ss, true), narrowing the window in which a user reads the old instance; the drift still hides that observation from the leader and, once compaction acts, removes the entries themselves.

The drift cannot be turned into new client values through the append path: append() refuses with PendingReconfigEntry while a StopSign is stored, which is the case throughout every observed drifted state, so the consequence set stays with index accounting, readability and compaction rather than with mis-assigned entries.

The lagging-replica loss of class (6) requires a snapshot-capable entry type whose snapshot can be built from an empty range; the non-snapshot variant of the same probe could not be executed at all, because snapshot() panics on that type for reasons independent of the drift (recorded under 40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-question-1).

The last executed state is not evidence of a limit: the decided index stopped following only because the reports outran a write quorum in that term, and no execution varied the number of replicas or the number of drifting reporters to see how that boundary moves.
limitations: The drift was exercised for eleven rounds with one mid-run leader change; that range found no bound and no repair, but the decided index stopped following once the reports outran every write quorum, so how far the decided index can keep following is a quorum property that was observed with one three-node pattern rather than characterised in general.
Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised; the producers observed are explicit reconnected() calls and an ordinary leader change onto a node that had already drifted.

Only three-node clusters were used, with in-memory storage, no persistence across restarts and one snapshot-capable entry type; the compaction witnesses depend on that entry type's snapshot semantics, and the entry type that cannot carry a snapshot aborts the compaction call instead of losing entries.

Several comparisons across the repeated-rounds, trim, snapshot, drift-bound and over-compaction receipts came out unknown because their admissions shared event names across cases in one execution or put a node condition on the prerequisite; those states are asserted from the sampled operands, with the violated comparisons cited above.

The cases sample after each drained round, so they do not show intermediate states inside a round, and no case exercised the forwarded compaction messages that a snapshot or trim call with local_only = false would send to peers; the peer-side variant is therefore argued from the per-node derivation of the bound and the range, not sampled.

The lagging-replica loss was observed once, with the leader's log empty above the compacted index, so whether a non-empty remainder would be handed over instead of an empty snapshot is not established; the receipt's own snapshot held zero ids.

The consequence set stays within index accounting, readability and compaction; the sealed configuration admits no further entries and refuses appends while the StopSign is stored, so no value is mis-assigned.

The routes by which a storage or caller could ask for a prefix below a compacted index by another entry point (a direct range read, a store-level trim, a peer whose recorded values were truthful) remain unexecuted, as recorded in the trim child's open gap.
interpretations.joint_history: Ten receipts of one harness lineage, each read on its own samples and never combined arithmetically: 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 (resync, control), 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 (single resync, read of index 6), 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 (newterm), dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea (staleleader), fd0b8be59c8f466fbf7768abb08f93b5 (snapshot-capable resync), 6c879304cdde4ddd8e1640207cdbf94d (three reconnection rounds), ec3329dc273e452aa92bcd44652c116a (drift then trim), e70b8baa087246c78ea3a64f24b8e97c (drift then snapshot), 2993c16874454f86a3f8b04364a00ef4 (drift-bound probe) and 0b9c22ae5fb043588aa7efa3ad009b25 (snapshot-capable over-compaction and the healthy NoSnapshot control). Each successor reproduces the earlier witnesses and adds cases; the two newest receipts come from the parent's own experiment 40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-experiment, which also carries the healthy control whose panic is recorded under 40ab66a5c5c847619ae2ff68b85641e7-question-1, and the two accounts the correction affected were reviewed in the same round as this one.
